title: Choose the visual world for the LLM Credit Risk Lab showcase
question: Re-roll dealt In Their Own Words. (The bolder catalog was unreachable, so this is a plain re-roll from grounded candidates.) Keep it, take the alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: In Their Own Words
options.lineage: 2007-2014 peer-to-peer loan listings, where borrowers pitched strangers in free text
options.thesis: The page is built from the borrowers' real sentences, and the model's reading is drawn directly onto them.
materials: oversized borrower sentences as the imagery
word-level heat from the model's coefficients
options.viewport: One real borrower sentence fills the screen at display scale over 125,700 drifting motes; words the model learned raise risk glow warm, words that lower it glow cool; beneath it the measured answer: +0.004 Gini, p = 0.079.
options.risk: Emotional quotes can upstage the rigor if the numbers arrive late, so the verdict sits in the first viewport.

options.label: The Lorenz Field
options.lineage: the CAP / Lorenz curve every credit modeler reads Gini from
options.thesis: Gini as literal geometry: 19,858 test loans sort themselves into the curve, and the area is the result.
materials: area fills as the only color
options.viewport: Loan motes fall into rank order and draw the E0 curve against the diagonal; the shaded area counts up to 0.417.
options.risk: A chart as hero is the familiar data-portfolio move; the most likely landing for this category.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The brief's own example played straight: obsidian ground, platinum text, one emerald accent, glass bento.
canonCard.viewport: Huge value proposition over a morphing glass orb, one glowing CTA.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every AI-startup landing page.
